No-Regret Learning in Stackelberg Security Games with an Unknown, Bounded Set of Attacker Types
radar.summary: In a repeated Stackelberg security game, a defender commits in every round to a randomized allocation of its resources, and an attacker, drawn from a set of types, best-responds. Existing no-regret guarantees assume that the defender knows this set of types in advance. We drop this assumption: the set of types is unknown, and its size is at most $K_{\max}$, an upper bound that the defender is not told. We show that what can be learned then depends on what the defender observes. If it observes the type of each attacker, an algorithm that adds types to its list as they appear achieves regret $\tilde O(nK_{\max}\sqrt{T})$ over $T$ rounds with $n$ targets, the same $\sqrt T$ rate as with known types, at an extra factor of only $\sqrt{K_{\max}}$ and without ever using $K_{\max}$. If it observes only the attacked target and types come from an infinite universe, no algorithm has sublinear regret: in a fixed three-target game every algorithm suffers regret at least $T-2$, even against a single attacker type, because it cannot tell which type it faces. If, in addition, it is told every $B$ rounds which types have appeared so far, sublinear regret returns, at $\tilde O(nK_{\max}^{4/3}T^{2/3}+K_{\max} B)$. The first term is the rate of the partial-information learner we use, and we show that the additive cost of the delay cannot be avoided.

radar.title: LLM-Guided Dual-Stage Latency Optimization for Closed-Loop 6G V2I Digital Twins
radar.summary: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

radar.title: A Comprehensive Review on Multi-Modal Large Language Models and Agentic Architectures for Precision Agricultural Decision Support
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: This article reviews recent developments in multi-modal large language models and agentic architectures for agricultural decision support. Forty-five representative studies published between 2023 and 2026 were selected across perception, language, orchestration, soil intelligence and governance, organised under a four-layer taxonomy, and classified against nine functional capabilities using a stated, reproducible procedure. The comparative analysis exposes a pronounced imbalance. Crop and disease perception is covered by 36 per cent of the selected studies, while dose-bearing prescription appears in 7 per cent, profit-aware recommendation in 4 per cent, and persistent per-field memory in a single study. Advisory tools in this literature therefore remain unable to exchange state: image-based scanners are rarely conditioned on measured soil chemistry, and crop-recommendation models optimise agronomic suitability without reference to farm economics. On this basis the article synthesises a conceptual reference architecture from the reviewed literature. It is a literature-derived synthesis rather than an implemented system, and calibrated abstention, evaluation protocols for longitudinal memory, and vernacular voice coverage emerge as the most urgent gaps.

radar.title: Multilisting for Horizontally Differentiated Services: Implications for Throughput and Social Welfare
radar.summary: When Joining More Queues Is Not Always Better When customers can join multiple wait lists, does more choice always improve a service system? In “Multilisting for Horizontally Differentiated Services: Implications for Throughput and Social Welfare,” Chen, Ding, and Yang study customers who can join several provider queues, choose only their preferred provider, or decline service. The authors compare this flexible multilisting design with single-listing and pooling. Multilisting attracts more customers and consistently achieves at least as much throughput as either alternative. It also improves social welfare relative to pooling. Yet compared with single-listing, the extra participation can worsen congestion and reduce welfare, even as access expands. The analysis further shows that the welfare-maximizing allocation may treat otherwise identical providers asymmetrically, and that nonnegative, asymmetric prices can steer customers toward socially efficient choices. The findings offer guidance for designing healthcare wait lists, public housing systems, vaccination programs, and other capacity-constrained services where access, matching, and congestion must be balanced.
